intro_en: In this lesson you will learn to count people and things in Japanese. Tamil adds a word for people when you count them (மூன்று பேர், three people). Japanese has a "counter word" for every kind of thing. You will use counters when you go shopping. You will also use them to say "how many times" or "how many hours". You will also learn some small words. だけ means "only" (மட்டும், only). ぐらい and ごろ mean "about" (சுமார், about).

g11-1.explanation_en: When you count things in Japanese, you add a "counter word" after the number. Tamil adds a counting word for people (பேர், as in மூன்று பேர், three people). Japanese has a word like this for every kind of thing. 〜人 (にん) is for people. 〜枚 (まい) is for flat things, like stamps, paper, photos and plates. 〜台 (だい) is for cars and machines. 〜本 (ほん) is for long, thin, round things, like pencils, umbrellas and flowers. 〜匹 (ひき) is for small animals. 〜冊 (さつ) is for books and notebooks. 〜個 (こ) is for small objects. 〜回 (かい) is for "times". 〜歳 (さい) is for age. 〜杯 (はい) is for cups and glasses. Sometimes you don’t know which counter to use. Then you can use 〜つ (ひとつ、ふたつ…) for general things. This set only goes up to ten. Its sounds come from the old Japanese numbers. Some forms are special: 一人 (ひとり), 二人 (ふたり) and 二十歳 (はたち). With 本, 匹, 杯, 個, 回 and 冊, the sound changes after 1, 3, 6, 8 and 10. For example: いっぽん、さんぼん、ろっぽん、はっぽん、じゅっぽん. Read the table below out loud and learn it by heart.
g11-1.tamil_parallel_en: Three people = 三人 (さんにん). Two cups of tea = お茶を二杯. Tamil uses பேர் (people) and கப் (cup) as counting words. In the same way, Japanese has a counter word for everything.
g11-1.formation_en:
Number + counter
〜つ (general things): ひとつ、ふたつ、みっつ、よっつ、いつつ、むっつ、ななつ、やっつ、ここのつ、とお (question: いくつ)
〜人 (people): ひとり、ふたり、さんにん、よにん、ごにん、ろくにん、しちにん / ななにん、はちにん、きゅうにん、じゅうにん (question: なんにん)
〜枚 (flat things): いちまい、にまい、さんまい、よんまい、ごまい、ろくまい、ななまい、はちまい、きゅうまい、じゅうまい (なんまい)
〜台 (cars, machines): いちだい、にだい、さんだい、よんだい、ごだい、ろくだい、ななだい、はちだい、きゅうだい、じゅうだい (なんだい)
〜本 (long things): いっぽん、にほん、さんぼん、よんほん、ごほん、ろっぽん、ななほん、はっぽん、きゅうほん、じゅっぽん (なんぼん)
〜匹 (small animals): いっぴき、にひき、さんびき、よんひき、ごひき、ろっぴき、ななひき、はっぴき、きゅうひき、じゅっぴき (なんびき)
〜冊 (books): いっさつ、にさつ、さんさつ、よんさつ、ごさつ、ろくさつ、ななさつ、はっさつ、きゅうさつ、じゅっさつ (なんさつ)
〜個 (small objects): いっこ、にこ、さんこ、よんこ、ごこ、ろっこ、ななこ、はっこ、きゅうこ、じゅっこ (なんこ)
〜回 (times): いっかい、にかい、さんかい、よんかい、ごかい、ろっかい、ななかい、はっかい、きゅうかい、じゅっかい (なんかい)
〜歳 (age): いっさい、にさい、さんさい、よんさい、ごさい、ろくさい、ななさい、はっさい、きゅうさい、じゅっさい、はたち (20) (なんさい / おいくつ)
〜杯 (cups, glasses): いっぱい、にはい、さんばい、よんはい、ごはい、ろっぱい、ななはい、はっぱい、きゅうはい、じゅっぱい (なんばい)
g11-1.pitfalls_en: Many people forget the sound changes, like いっぽん and さんぼん. They wrongly say いちほん or さんほん. Only 一人 and 二人 are special: ひとり and ふたり. From three on, it is さんにん, よにん. Say よにん, not よんにん.

g11-2.explanation_en: In Japanese, the amount (number + counter) usually comes right before the verb (the action word). For example: りんごを三つ買います. The particle を comes after the thing. But no particle comes after the amount. So you must not say 三つを. Tamil has the same order (ஆப்பிளை மூன்று வாங்கினேன், I bought three apples). The object ending (-ஐ) comes after the thing. The number (மூன்று, three) stands alone before the verb. The same order is used with が and あります / います: 猫が三匹います. You can also say "a few" or "a lot". Put 少し or たくさん in this same place.
g11-2.tamil_parallel_en: மிட்டாயை மூன்று வாங்கினேன் ("I bought three sweets") = 飴を三つ買いました. In both languages the amount stands alone, right before the verb.
g11-2.formation_en:
N + を + [number + counter] + V ます
N + が + [number + counter] + あります / います
g11-2.pitfalls_en: Don’t put a particle after the amount. 三つを買います and 三人が来ます are wrong. "Three friends came" = 友達が三人来ました. The amount goes right before the verb.

g11-3.explanation_en: To ask "how many", put 何 (なん) before the counter. For example: 何人 (なんにん), 何枚 (なんまい), 何台, 何本, 何匹, 何冊, 何個, 何回, 何歳. Only the 〜つ group has its own word: いくつ. To ask someone’s age politely, you can also say おいくつですか. To ask "how long" or "how much time", use どのぐらい (or どのくらい). Tamil has two different words here. "How many" is for things you can count (எத்தனை). "How much" is for amounts and time (எவ்வளவு). Japanese is the same. 何 + counter = how many (எத்தனை). どのぐらい = how much or how long (எவ்வளவு). The question word comes before the verb. It goes in the same place as the amount.
g11-3.tamil_parallel_en: மாணவர்கள் எத்தனை பேர் இருக்கிறார்கள்? ("How many students are there?") = 学生が何人いますか. எவ்வளவு நேரம்? ("How long?") = どのぐらいですか
g11-3.formation_en:
何 + counter (何人 / 何枚 / 何台 / 何本 / 何匹 / 何冊 / 何個 / 何回 / 何歳)
いくつ (〜つ group; age: おいくつ)
どのぐらい / どのくらい (time, amount)
g11-3.pitfalls_en: Use いくつ only for the 〜つ group and for age. Don’t ask about people with いくつ. Ask 何人. "How much" for a price is いくら (Lesson 3). "How long" is どのぐらい. Don’t mix them up.

g11-4.explanation_en: "At three o’clock" and "for three hours" are different. 三時 (さんじ) is a point in time (o’clock). 三時間 (さんじかん) is a length of time (hours). Adding 間 (かん) makes it a length of time. In the same way, 一週間 (いっしゅうかん) = one week (length). 一か月 (いっかげつ) = one month (length). 一年 (いちねん) = one year. For days, use the same readings as for dates (ふつか、みっか…). They work for lengths of time too. There is one difference. "One day" = 一日 (いちにち). But the date "the 1st" is ついたち. This is very important: に comes after a point in time (三時に起きます). But に does not come after a length of time (三時間勉強します). Tamil works the same way. "At three o’clock" takes an ending (மூன்று மணிக்கு, with -க்கு). But "I studied for three hours" has no ending (மூன்று மணி நேரம் படித்தேன்). A length of time also comes before the verb.
g11-4.tamil_parallel_en: மூன்று மணிக்கு எழுந்தேன் ("I got up at three") = 三時に起きました (point in time, with に). மூன்று மணி நேரம் படித்தேன் ("I studied for three hours") = 三時間勉強しました (length of time, no に). Tamil -க்கு works just like に here.
g11-4.formation_en:
〜時間 (hours): いちじかん、にじかん、さんじかん、よじかん、ごじかん、ろくじかん、しちじかん、はちじかん、くじかん、じゅうじかん (なんじかん)
〜日 (days): いちにち、ふつか、みっか、よっか、いつか、むいか、なのか、ようか、ここのか、とおか (なんにち)
〜週間 (weeks): いっしゅうかん、にしゅうかん、さんしゅうかん、よんしゅうかん、ごしゅうかん、ろくしゅうかん、ななしゅうかん、はっしゅうかん、きゅうしゅうかん、じゅっしゅうかん (なんしゅうかん)
〜か月 (months): いっかげつ、にかげつ、さんかげつ、よんかげつ、ごかげつ、ろっかげつ、ななかげつ、はっかげつ、きゅうかげつ、じゅっかげつ (なんかげつ)
〜年 (years): いちねん、にねん、さんねん、よねん、ごねん、ろくねん、ななねん、はちねん、きゅうねん、じゅうねん (なんねん)
Length of time + V (no に); question: どのぐらい / 何時間 / 何日 …
g11-4.pitfalls_en: Don’t put に after a length of time. 三時間に勉強します is wrong. に is only for a point in time. 四時間 = よじかん (not よんじかん). 九時間 = くじかん.

g11-5.explanation_en: To say "twice a week", put に after the time period. Then add 〜回 (かい): 一週間に二回. Here に means "per" (Tamil -க்கு, as in வாரத்திற்கு, per week). It works with every length of time. 一日に三回 = three times a day. 一か月に一回 = once a month. 一年に二回 = twice a year. To ask, say 一週間に何回 (how many times a week). To say "not even once", use 全然 + a negative (Lesson 9). Like other amounts, 〜回 comes before the verb.
g11-5.tamil_parallel_en: வாரத்திற்கு இரண்டு முறை படம் பார்க்கிறேன் ("I watch a film twice a week") = 一週間に二回映画を見ます. Here に does the job of Tamil -க்கு ("per").
g11-5.formation_en:
[length of time] + に + [number + 回] + V
一日に / 一週間に / 一か月に / 一年に + 一回、二回、三回 … (question: 何回)
g11-5.pitfalls_en: Don’t use で, as in 一週間で二回. For "per", use に. Many people also leave out に, as in 一週間二回. That is wrong too.

g11-6.explanation_en: だけ means "only". It is the same as the Tamil word (மட்டும்). Put it after a noun (a thing word) or an amount. It means "just that, nothing more". After だけ, を or は is usually dropped: コーヒーだけ飲みます ("I drink only coffee"). Other particles like に or で can come after だけ (日曜日だけ休みます). With amounts: 一つだけ (only one), 二人だけ (only two people). In Tamil you say "only one" (ஒன்று மட்டும்) or "only me" (நான் மட்டும்). だけ goes in the same place and has the same meaning.
g11-6.tamil_parallel_en: காபி மட்டும் குடிக்கிறேன் ("I drink only coffee") = コーヒーだけ飲みます. இரண்டு பேர் மட்டும் வந்தார்கள் ("Only two people came") = 二人だけ来ました. だけ sits in the same place as Tamil மட்டும்.
g11-6.formation_en:
N + だけ (+ V): を / は are usually dropped
[number + counter] + だけ
N + だけ + です
g11-6.pitfalls_en: Don’t put だけ after the verb. 飲みますだけ is wrong. だけ must come right after the word that "only" is about.

g11-7.explanation_en: In Tamil, "about" is one word (சுமார்). You use it for "about three o’clock" and for "about three hours". But Japanese has two words. ごろ is only for a point in time. 三時ごろ = at about three o’clock. 五月ごろ = around May. ぐらい (or くらい) is for amounts, numbers, lengths of time and prices. 三時間ぐらい = about three hours. 十人ぐらい = about ten people. 千円ぐらい = about 1,000 yen. Here is a simple rule. Use ごろ after a time that could take に. Use ぐらい after an amount. After ごろ you can drop に (三時ごろ起きます). In questions you will also see どのぐらい, いくつぐらい and 何人ぐらい.
g11-7.tamil_parallel_en: சுமார் மூன்று மணிக்கு ("at about three o’clock") = 三時ごろ (point in time). சுமார் மூன்று மணி நேரம் ("about three hours") = 三時間ぐらい (amount). Tamil uses one word, சுமார், for both. Japanese uses two.
g11-7.formation_en:
[point in time] + ごろ (に can be dropped)
[number / length of time / price] + ぐらい / くらい
g11-7.pitfalls_en: Don’t use ごろ with an amount. 三時間ごろ and 十人ごろ are wrong. Amounts always take ぐらい. People sometimes say 三時ぐらい when they talk. But in the exam, write ごろ for a point in time.

items.L11-q01: 切手 = きって (ஸ்டாம்பு, stamp). It has a small っ. きて is wrong because the っ is missing.
items.L11-q02: 封筒 = ふうとう (envelope). It has two long sounds: ふう and とう. ふとう and ふうと are wrong. Each one is missing a long sound.
items.L11-q03: 二人 has a special reading: ふたり (இரண்டு பேர், two people). It is not ににん. 〜人 (にん) is only used from three people (さんにん) on.
items.L11-q04: はがき = 葉書 (போஸ்ட் கார்டு, postcard). It comes from 葉 (leaf) + 書 (writing). 菜書 has 菜 (vegetable), a kanji that looks similar. Be careful.
items.L11-q05: The counter for books, さつ, is written 冊. 二枚 (にまい) is for flat things. 册 and 卅 only look similar.
items.L11-q06: Books take 〜冊 (さつ). 三本 is for long, thin, round things. 三枚 is for flat things.
items.L11-q07: To ask how many people, use 何人 (なんにん, எத்தனை பேர், how many people). いくつ is for things and age. We don’t use it for people.
items.L11-q08: Cars and machines take 〜台 (だい). 二匹 is for small animals.
items.L11-q09: 十一時 is a point in time. So "about" is ごろ (சுமார், about). ぐらい is for amounts (十一時間ぐらい).
items.L11-q10: "My younger sister is twenty years old." The age is 二十歳 (はたち, இருபது வயது, twenty years old). The other three are counters for things, times and cars.
items.L11-q11: "In the morning I drink only tea." Only = だけ (மட்டும்). ずつ (வீதம், each) only goes with an amount.
items.L11-q12: Twice a week = two days in the week (Monday and Thursday). 一か月に二回 means twice a month. That is a different time period.
items.L11-q13: "There is only a cat" means there is no dog. 猫がいません has the opposite meaning. だけ (மட்டும், only) is not a negative.
items.L11-q14: 三時間ぐらい = about three hours (சுமார் மூன்று மணி நேரம்) = だいたい三時間. 三時ごろ means "at about three o’clock". That is a point in time, not an amount.
items.L11-q15: An amount comes alone before the verb, with no particle after it. 切手を already has を. So adding を again in 三枚を is wrong.
items.L11-q16: "Three times a week": use に after the time period. It works like the Tamil ending (-க்கு, "per"). で is for places and tools. It doesn’t fit here.
items.L11-q17: 八時間 is a length of time, so に does not come after it. 八時に (at eight o’clock) needs に. But 時間 (hours) does not.
items.L11-q18: How many people in the family? For people, use 何人 (なんにん, எத்தனை பேர், how many people). いくつ is not used for people.
items.L11-q19: 一時間 is a length of time. So "about" is ぐらい (சுமார், about). ごろ is only for a point in time (一時ごろ).
items.L11-q20: "How many times a year" = 一年に何回 (வருடத்திற்கு எத்தனை முறை). 何回に is wrong. に is already in 一年に, so don’t add it again.
items.L11-q21: "One postcard each for everyone" = 一枚ずつ (ஒன்று வீதம், one each). ぐらい would mean "about one". That doesn’t fit the meaning.
items.L11-q22: 八十円の切手を (80 யென் ஸ்டாம்பை, the 80-yen stamps) → 五枚 (ஐந்து, five) → 買いました. The amount comes right before the verb.
items.L11-q23: 一週間に二回 (வாரத்திற்கு இரண்டு முறை, twice a week) → 家族に (குடும்பத்திற்கு, to my family) → 電話をかけます. 〜回 comes right after the time period.
items.L11-q24: 毎晩十一時ごろ (தினமும் இரவு சுமார் 11 மணிக்கு, every night at about 11) → 牛乳を一杯飲みます. ごろ comes after the time. 一杯 comes before the verb.
items.L11-q25: [1] The younger sister’s age = 二十歳 (はたち, இருபது வயது, twenty). [2] A cat is a small animal → 二匹 (இரண்டு, two). 二人 is for people. [3] "Twice a week" is a habit → use the present form かけます. かけました is past, so it doesn’t fit a habit.
